answer: Agents could require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation or place bids. A shared registry checks that the same stake is not backing multiple identities; proven fraud burns it, while honest participation unlocks it later. A cipher may hide personal details without hiding stake ownership, even as identities drift through a nebula of aliases. The delta for an attacker is concrete: every extra identity needs fresh capital at risk.
